title: Kale, fresh, cooked, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Kale (Brassica oleracea var. acephala) is a leafy cruciferous vegetable. Fresh kale has dark green, slightly curly leaves with a mildly bitter flavor. When cooked without added fat, it retains most of its nutrients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Kale is often called a "superfood" because of its high vitamin and mineral content.
In the wild it grows along the Mediterranean coast and on Atlantic islands.
Leaves can be smooth or curly; curly kale is frequently considered more nutrient‑dense.
Traditional medicine has used kale to support digestion and bone health.
In Japan kale is known as "mizuna" and is a common addition to miso soup.

items.title: Rich in vitamin K
items.content: Kale provides over 700% of the daily value for vitamin K, essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: High in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and enhances iron absorption.

items.title: Abundant antioxidants
items.content: Kale contains carotenoids, quercetin, and sulforaphane, which protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Good source of fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and helps maintain healthy blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Kale supplies calcium, magnesium, and iron, important for bones, muscles, and blood formation.

items.title: Interaction with blood thinners
items.content: The high vitamin K content may reduce the effectiveness of anticoagulant medications.

items.title: Oxalates
items.content: Kale contains oxalates, which can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

items.title: Thyroid considerations
items.content: Glucosinolates in kale may affect thyroid function when consumed in very large amounts.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Kale can be eaten raw in salads, but for fat‑free cooking steam, blanch, or dry‑sauté it. Remove tough stems, slice the leaves, and season with lemon juice, garlic, or a splash of soy sauce. Cooked kale pairs well with beans, quinoa, or roasted vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh kale in the refrigerator in a perforated bag or wrapped in a damp towel; it stays crisp for 3‑5 days. Cooked kale should be kept in an airtight container in the fridge and consumed within 2‑3 days.
